What happens to my Microsoft / Outlook when I die?

Short answer: Microsoft generally won't release a deceased person's Outlook.com or OneDrive content to next of kin without a valid court order or subpoena. Microsoft accounts can also be closed after long periods of inactivity. If you set up OneDrive's digital legacy feature, a trusted contact can request read-only access.

What to do

  1. Check Microsoft's 'Preserve your digital legacy with OneDrive' page and set up a trusted contact if it's available to you.
  2. Store your Microsoft password in a password manager with emergency access.
  3. Export important email and files periodically.
  4. After a death, follow Microsoft's official guidance; expect to need legal documents.

Read the official policy ↗

FAQ

Can I get into my late parent's Outlook account?

Usually only with a court order, unless a legacy feature or password was planned in advance.
